newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday, June 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday, June 26.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* The European Union's monetary committee urged Italy to make additional reforms to its pensions systems. Meeting to review the country's efforts to consolidate its public finances ahead of economic and monetary union, the commission was generally pleased by Rome's efforts and economic targets for the next three years (all).

* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said Italy would certainly be a EMU member from the start. He said Italy's target of 1.8 percent average inflation next year was credible and stability and strength of the lira raised expectations of a fall in short-term interest rates. He said the spread between Italian government 10-year bonds (Btp) and German 10-year bunds could fall further and a cut in official interest rates was more likely given the healthy state of the economy (all).

* Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said Italian official interest rates would not fall to the levels of German interest rates as the lira was not as stable and appreciated currency as the German mark. Fazio also said that banks should cut labour and other costs rapidly in order to boost profitability (all).
* Enrico Bondi, managing director of agri-industrial group Montedison, said Montedison's gross operating margin rose 13.5 percent to 1.5 trillion lire in the first five months of 1997.
* A quarterly report by national statistics institute Istat showed Italian unemployment rose to 12.5 percent in April against 12.4 percent in January (all).
* Italian government intends to privatise Banca Nazionale del Lavoro once it has been merged with Banco di Napoli.
* Mediobanca's central director of finance Gerardo Braggiotti is to remain at the merchant bank, after reports he was on the verge of leaving (Il Sole).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
